evidence: io.lisp:2537-2542: `(fnn-octets-clear) ... (fnn-octets-reserve (min (max 0 (sb-posix:stat-size st)) bound))` followed by appending every chunk. Only fnn-state-checkpoint-load-arena calls `(fnn-octets-release)` (io.lisp:2669, 2675). The :refused branch at io.lisp:2605-2606 and the decode-refusal branch at io.lisp:2618 `(values (if (equal answer '(:refused :arena)) :arena :refused) 0)` return without releasing.
fix: Call fnn-octets-release on every exit from fnn-state-checkpoint-load (an unwind-protect around the plan and decode), not only after the arena path.
reviewer: fnn-state-checkpoint-plan reserves min(file size, fn-store-sco-file-read-bound) in the served octet buffer (io.lisp:2537-2542) and appends chunks into it. The :refused branches of fnn-state-checkpoint-load (io.lisp:2605-2606) and the decode-refusal branch (io.lisp:2618) return without calling fnn-octets-release. The only releases are in fnn-state-checkpoint-load-arena (io.lisp:2669, 2675). The array is kept because fnn-octets-clear only resets the count (io.lisp:238-240). This is reached only with a corrupt, oversized or wrong-schema checkpoint, so it is rare, but it is the retention fnn-octets-release's docstring (io.lisp:257-262) says it prevents.
scenario: The checkpoint is truncated, exceeds a bound, has another schema, or lacks the arena run. The open falls back to full replay, but the served attempt's buffer keeps an array as large as the checkpoint file, up to fn-store-sco-file-read-bound (hundreds of MB on a large store). It stays for the life of the owner, because served attempts only ever grow the buffer. fnn-octets-release's own docstring describes exactly this retention as the thing it exists to prevent.
title: A refused or corrupt state checkpoint leaves a file-sized array in the served octet buffer
